sources.title: o3-deep-research model reference
sources.evidence: The exact model reference identifies alias o3-deep-research and default snapshot o3-deep-research-2025-06-26. It documents 200,000 context tokens, text/image input, text output, reasoning, prompt caching and hosted research tools. The current Markdown reference marks both model and snapshot Shut down. It supplies no total or active parameter count. Parameter re-audit October 27: reopened the exact documentation and read the full Markdown reference freshly fetched with HTTP 200 at 16:22:46 UTC; its numeric tables concern tokens, prices and rate limits, not model weights.

sources.title: Introducing deep research
sources.evidence: The contemporaneous page is dated February 2, 2025 and launches deep research in ChatGPT for Pro users. It describes an early/upcoming o3 variant trained for browsing and data analysis, including Python. Later updates and the lightweight o4-mini version are distinct from this original release. Read through the indexed primary page; a separate direct HTTP fetch returned 403. Reopened October 27 through the web reader, including the explicit upcoming-o3 relationship and end-to-end reinforcement-learning description; the fresh direct 403 is an access limitation, not evidence that a count is absent.

sources.title: Deep research in the API, webhooks, and web search with o3
sources.evidence: The June 26, 2025 announcement explicitly identifies o3-deep-research and o4-mini-deep-research as the same deep research models already available in ChatGPT, now offered in the API. Read the original first post through the topic JSON; its author is Nikunj Handa and the metadata identifies OpenAI Staff and administrator. This binds the research-model lineage, without proving byte-identical February and June checkpoints.

sources.title: Deep Research System Card, February 25, 2025
sources.evidence: Parameter re-audit October 27: reopened the original PDF and inspected the complete text freshly fetched with HTTP 200 at 15:42:50 UTC. Sections 1-2 identify an early o3 version optimized through reinforcement learning on browsing/Python research tasks. This is explicit named lineage, not mere family resemblance; these sections report no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or other structural resizing, but provide no nominal base or variant count to inherit. Section 3.2 separately identifies an o3-mini chain-of-thought summarizer. Full-text count/activation and structural-change searches and the research-model comparison tables establish neither total nor active size. URL, sampling and evaluation parameters are not weight counts.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: The June 2025 section places the release of o3-deep-research and o4-mini-deep-research under June 24, while listing June 26 snapshot identifiers. This conflicts with the June 26 contemporaneous API announcement, so the snapshot suffix alone cannot settle the API launch day. Both are later than the original ChatGPT research-model release.

sources.title: Deep research API guide
sources.evidence: The reference describes web search, file search, specialized MCP search/fetch servers and code interpreter support for the exact model. It explicitly excludes other tools such as custom function calling. Its introductory retirement notice retains examples for reference after July 23, 2026; these examples are not evidence of current endpoint operation.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 notice states that access to o3-deep-research and o3-deep-research-2025-06-26 shut down on July 23, 2026. The replacement listed is gpt-5.6-sol. This exact alias/snapshot notice controls over an older indexed model-page Deprecated label.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: This archived engineering recipe expressly applies to models before GPT-5.6. Section 2.1 explains that prompt caching reuses key/value projections in Transformer attention layers. Combined with the exact o3-deep-research reference’s explicit prompt-caching support, this supports a qualified broad Transformer inference, not a dense/MoE topology or parameter count.

sources.title: ChatGPT Agent System Card, July 17, 2025
sources.evidence: Parameter re-audit October 27: reopened the original PDF and full text freshly fetched with HTTP 200 at 15:42:50 UTC. Section 1 identifies ChatGPT agent as a new model in the o3 family. Table 6 explicitly compares Deep research, but its columns are multilingual performance scores, not total or active parameter counts. Full-text count/activation searches provide no parameter convention for the original research variant; the new agent does not redefine it.

sources.title: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini System Card, April 16, 2025
sources.evidence: Parameter re-audit October 27: reopened the original PDF and full text freshly fetched with HTTP 200 at 15:42:49 UTC. Section 2 describes reasoning-model training, and later sections cite deep research safety evaluations. Neither the training text nor the model comparison tables publish a nominal total or active count for base o3 or o3-deep-research. The base-o3/o4-mini performance columns do not establish research-variant size.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Parameter re-audit October 27: reopened the OpenAI-authored arXiv report, revised May 1, 2026, and inspected its full PDF text freshly fetched with HTTP 200 at 15:42:39 UTC. Table 1 maps base o3 and o3 Pro to GPT-5 successors; Section 2 and the later safety/performance comparisons do not publish base-o3 or o3-deep-research total/active counts. No exact research-variant parameter row or active-count convention was found.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The agreement governs hosted API service access, grants access/use rights and retains OpenAI intellectual-property rights. Together with the exact hosted model reference and launch, this supports the descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open checkpoint license. Read the indexed primary text; direct HTTP fetch returned 403.

sources.title: File inputs API guide
sources.evidence: The guide explains that PDF input is parsed into extracted text and page images for vision-capable models. File processing is distinct from a native PDF encoder or image generation. No audio/video input or image output is established for the exact research model.

sources.title: Introduction to the Deep Research API
sources.evidence: The archived recipe names o3-deep-research-2025-06-26 and distinguishes it from the lighter o4-mini-deep-research snapshot. Its code demonstrates Responses API web search, reasoning summaries and optional code interpreter. The recipe is historical and does not establish current availability.

sources.title: Models.dev upstream record
sources.evidence: The inspected upstream lead labels the family o, uses June 26, 2025 as the API release and gives 200,000 context, image/text input and reasoning/tools. Its catalog claims were checked against the primary sources above; it is not the basis for the revised earliest release or architecture.

sources.title: o3 model reference, Markdown

The explicit early-o3 lineage therefore has no supported numerical size anchor in this source.

sources.title: DeepSearchQA: Bridging the Comprehensiveness Gap for Deep Research Agents, December 11, 2025

Section 4 and Table 4 (PDF page 8) include an exact o3 Deep Research row, separate from o4 Mini Deep Research, with fully correct/incorrect, extraneous-answer and F1 metrics. There is no total/activated-parameter column or numerical size for this model. This is an original later research comparison, not an OpenAI size disclosure.

sources.title: Tongyi DeepResearch Technical Report, November 15, 2025
sources.evidence: Freshly downloaded the team-hosted complete PDF October 27 at 17:20:58 UTC with HTTP 200; the web PDF reader rejected its octet-stream content type, so the successfully fetched PDF was parsed locally. Section 4.1 and Table 1 distinguish base OpenAI o3 from OpenAI DeepResearch. The table reports benchmark results, not size. The abstract and Sections 1/4 disclose 30.5B total and 3.3B activated only for Tongyi DeepResearch; those values cannot be transferred to the OpenAI comparison rows.

sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 after fresh exact-model total/active-parameter searches surfaced the page. Its Supported Parameters list describes API request controls, not trainable weights.

name.note: Exact research-model alias; the API reference binds it to o3-deep-research-2025-06-26. It is distinct from base o3, o3-pro and o4-mini-deep-research.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes the model reference, original announcement and research-system card.

family.note: Use the documented o3 lineage instead of the broad o-series prefix. The original research variant used an early o3 model; the separate o3-mini summarizer is not the model being indexed.

release_date.note: Earliest public availability of the o3 research variant was the February 2 ChatGPT launch. The later official API announcement explicitly binds o3-deep-research to that ChatGPT research offering. This is a product-lineage date, not a claim that the June 26 API checkpoint existed in February. The current changelog says June 24 for API release while the contemporaneous API announcement is June 26; preserve that conflict separately.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is a hosted OpenAI service; the accessed primary release and model reference provide no downloadable checkpoint or open-weight grant.

license.note: Descriptive licensing classification for hosted API access under OpenAI terms. This is not an open-source model-weight license or a claim that service outputs are owned by OpenAI.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 original-source and exact-model searches found no supported nominal total. The early-o3 relationship and research RL training are explicit and do not report structural resizing, but no supported nominal o3 count is available to inherit. Later OpenAI, Google and Tongyi comparison tables report performance without this model's size. Benchable's 400B lead is expressly a rumor; the separate o3-mini summarizer is excluded.

active_parameters_b.note: Separately searched active/activated counts and later original model-team comparison tables on October 27. No numerical active count or activation convention for o3-deep-research or a supported base-o3 active count was found. Google DeepSearchQA Table 4 and Tongyi Table 1 supply performance only; Tongyi's 3.3B belongs to its own model. Neither dense-equals-total nor an API request-parameter list establishes an active weight count.

architecture.note: Qualified architectural inference: this exact model explicitly supports prompt caching, and OpenAI’s applicable pre-GPT-5.6 engineering recipe describes that mechanism as caching Transformer attention key/value projections. This supports only the broad Transformer label. Exact variant training/interpretability searches and the accessed reports did not establish dense/MoE structure, layer counts, expert routing or the complete multimodal topology.

context_window.note: Last documented API context in tokens for the alias/default June 26 snapshot, distinct from the separately listed 100,000-token output cap. This value is not asserted for the original February ChatGPT deployment. The API model shut down on July 23, 2026.

modalities.note: The exact API model reference documents text/image input and file uploads. The API file-input guide documents PDF support for vision-capable models through extracted text and page images. Include pdf as a supported input format, not as a native PDF encoder. Python plots or embedded web images are tool artifacts, not native image output. No audio/video capability is established.

reasoning.note: The exact API reference documents reasoning-token support. The original card describes reinforcement learning for multi-step research reasoning; this is distinct from the separate o3-mini summarizer used in ChatGPT.

tool_call.note: True for documented web search, file search, code interpreter and constrained MCP search/fetch calls. Custom function calling and arbitrary MCP interfaces are explicitly unsupported. These are last documented capabilities, not a claim that the retired endpoint accepts requests.

patch.notes: The release date is the February 2, 2025 ChatGPT debut of the o3 research variant. OpenAI’s later API announcement identifies o3-deep-research as the same ChatGPT research offering. The June 26 API snapshot is a later identifier; checkpoint identity across those dates is not established. The current API changelog lists June 24, while the contemporaneous API announcement is dated June 26. The 200,000-token context and text/image input specifications describe the last documented API snapshot, o3-deep-research-2025-06-26, not necessarily the original ChatGPT deployment. OpenAI shut down the alias and dated API snapshot on July 23, 2026. Tool support covers web search, file search, code interpreter and MCP search/fetch. Custom function calling and arbitrary MCP tool interfaces are unsupported. PDF processing and Python-generated figures are service/tool capabilities, not additional native modalities. Transformer is a broad inference from exact-model prompt-caching support and OpenAI’s applicable engineering explanation. Dense/MoE structure and nominal total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed. The documented early-o3 lineage cannot yield a nominal size because no supported o3 count is published. The separate o3-mini chain-of-thought summarizer is excluded from this model’s specifications.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening the original training/lineage sources and later OpenAI, Google DeepSearchQA and Tongyi research comparisons. Named early-o3 lineage is established, but no supported base count can be inherited; the explicit 400B rumor is rejected. Added explicit null parameter patch values and preserved the other 12 field assessments, including the February product-lineage release, June API-date conflict, shutdown and historical capability scope.
